key_insight: AA-ViT uses anatomical, structural, and frequency guidance in a vision transformer to synthesize contrast-enhanced brain MRI from routine pre-contrast scans while better preserving lesion and tissue boundaries.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this could reduce reliance on gadolinium contrast agents, shorten MRI workflows, and improve access for patients who cannot receive contrast.
method: Vision transformer for contrast-enhanced MRI synthesis
Guided by anatomical structure and frequency information
Uses T1, T2, and FLAIR as inputs
evidence_signal: On BraTS 2021, the model outperformed state-of-the-art methods on PSNR and SSIM, and three neuroradiologists plus one neurosurgeon gave 19 random cases a mean clinical score of 3.94/5.
watch_item: The clinical evaluation was small and preliminary, so broader external validation is needed before considering routine use.
paper_title: AA-ViT: Anatomically Aware Vision Transformer with Structural and Frequency Guidance for Contrast Enhanced Brain MRI Synthesis
